title: PacketListRecord: add an ensureColorized() method and use it.
description:
Don't call the columnString() and discard the result in order to force colorization; instead, add a separate method to force colorization and use that.
    
This avoids the need to choose a column; we were using 1 as the column number, but column numbers are zero-origin, so that's column 2, whichisn't guaranteed to exist (a crash ensued if it didn't).

notes.body:
@geraldcombs, this came from commit 255d53dfc11fa49eadd30fefe3ed5950b03e6659.

What is that call to `record->columnString()` supposed to do?  If it's supposed to force a redirect to colorize the row, there needs to be a way to do so without depending on a particular column requiring a redirect (much less depending on there being more than one column; I discovered the crash when running Wireshark with the option `-o "gui.column.format:No.,%t"`, when testing to make sure you don't need to quote the strings in the value of gui.column.format unless they contain characters such as a comma).

> If it's supposed to force a redirect to colorize the row

It looks like that's the case, specifically that record->columnString() was and still is a cheap way to trigger redissection with colorization.
I think so.
Any preferences for the method name?
Maybe ensureDissected or ensureDissectedAndColorized? We tend to use "ensure" elsewhere in the code base.

It's checking the status of various colorized indications before dissecting, so `ensureDissected()` is probably not correct; I'd go for `ensureColorized()` or `ensureDissectedAndColorized()`.  The dissection is done to evaluate the packet-matching expressions in the coloring rules, so would `ensureColorized()` suffice?
`ensureColorized()` sounds fine to me.
OK, so how's this?
LGTM. Thanks!
